name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: 11 Sep: IRGC claims a strike on a US Saildrone-type UUV in Hormuz; UKMTO reports two vessels hit off Oman by projectiles. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao confirmed on the record that Iran 'blew the hell out of' the Fifth Fleet's Bahrain base (28 Feb 2026 damage, no return timeline). GCC and Iranian foreign ministers are scheduled to meet in Salalah, Oman on 14 Sep — the war's first ministerial-level dialogue. Kpler (~13/day 10-day avg) and Lloyd's List Intelligence (~12/day) now converge closely on Hormuz transit volume, partially narrowing (not resolving) the gap with the 'effectively closed' insurance-based reading and a lower single-day (7 transits) figure. A reported, unconfirmed thermal/fire event near Saudi Arabia's East-West 'Petroline' pipeline (a Hormuz-bypass route) surfaced 10 Sep but largely matches known flare sites.
importance: Critical — the sharpest and most information-dense window of the reignited U.S.-Iran conflict to date, now combining continued attempted strikes (including on unmanned assets), an official U.S. admission of degraded Gulf basing, and the war's first genuine multilateral diplomatic opening.
assessment: A genuinely two-track posture has emerged: continued Iranian claim/attempt activity (now extending to unmanned US assets) running in parallel with a real, if fragile, Gulf-brokered diplomatic channel. The Bahrain admission confirms degraded U.S. forward posture is a durable fact, not a contested claim. Independent AIS-based Hormuz-transit trackers are converging for the first time, a modest but genuine step toward data reconciliation. Miscalculation risk remains materially elevated heading into the 14 Sep meeting.
lastChange: 2026-09-11 — IRGC claims an 11 Sep Saildrone-UUV strike; UKMTO reports two vessels hit off Oman; Acting Navy Secretary Cao confirms Bahrain base damage on the record; a 14 Sep GCC-Iran ministerial meeting in Salalah, Oman is announced; Kpler/Lloyd's List transit data converges around ~12-13/day; unconfirmed East-West pipeline thermal activity surfaces.
orgRelevance: Reassess Hormuz-transit shipping, insurance, personnel, and supply-chain exposure against the officially-confirmed degraded U.S. Gulf posture; watch the 14 Sep Salalah meeting as the nearest-term potential inflection before revising contingency posture; plan against the ~12-13/day AIS-tracker range as the better-supported transit figure.
nextIndicator: CENTCOM confirmation or denial of the 11 Sep Saildrone claim; outcome of the 14 Sep Salalah meeting; any Saudi confirmation regarding the East-West pipeline; continued Kpler/Lloyd's List convergence.

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: China's military-affiliated license-denial rule (since 1 Dec 2025) and the June 2026 entity-list targeting of MP Materials/USA Rare Earth remain the binding constraints; no new PRC action confirmed this cycle. The broader Oct 2025 rare-earth controls remain suspended until their 10 Nov 2026 expiry, now roughly two months out.
importance: Critical — binding, targeted constraint on munitions/platform output and the domestic-substitution response itself, now compounded by active Hormuz-theater munitions consumption and a newly surfaced Navy-shipbuilding demand vector.
assessment: Durable, weaponizable chokepoint at its already-escalated severity; no signal of near-term relaxation ahead of the 10 Nov suspension-expiry decision or the 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit. Structural risk remains HIGH; near-term program impact MODERATE-to-HIGH given entity-list targeting, rising Hormuz-theater munitions consumption, and now a third demand vector from the CVN-81 steam-catapult/elevator redesign.
lastChange: 2026-09-11 — no new PRC action this cycle; continuity at the escalated severity. Separately (cross-linked, not a rare-earth action itself), Iran's capture of a defective Anduril Dive-LD UUV near Hormuz adds a narrow hardware/technology-exposure angle to the DIB's supply-chain risk picture alongside the materials chokepoint.
orgRelevance: Map magnet exposure in hardware BOMs against named entities; pursue second sources, including newer SRM/munitions entrants (Anduril, Ursa Major, X-Bow) and any carrier-catapult/elevator-adjacent suppliers, outside China-targeted firms.
nextIndicator: DoD mine-to-magnet award cadence and FORGE-initiative disbursement; any further PRC entity-list or licensing action; the 10 Nov 2026 suspension-expiry decision; rare-earth movement at or around the 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit.

name: Actively Exploited Edge / AI-Infra / Windows CVEs
status: CISA added the MikroTik 'MikroTrick' chain (CVE-2026-67277, CVE-2026-86060) to KEV on 10 Sep, closing an 8-day gap since CERT Polska's advisory. A CVSS-10.0 Cisco Firewall Management Center bypass (CVE-2026-20079, Cisco aware of exploitation since August) and Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2026-19490, CVSS 9.3) carry a federal 12 Sep patch deadline alongside Fortinet — six vendor families (SonicWall, Fortinet, Citrix, Cisco, MikroTik, plus Windows/N-able) added to KEV within roughly three weeks.
importance: High — trust-boundary, perimeter/authentication, endpoint, and MSP/RMM-supply-chain components common in enterprise and DIB networks, now spanning six distinct vendor families in under three weeks with a maximum-severity flaw and an imminent federal deadline.
assessment: The MikroTik gap is closed, but the cohort widened again with a CVSS-10.0 Cisco FMC bypass under a hard, two-day-out federal deadline. The density, maximum-severity scoring, and six-vendor spread in under three weeks continues to indicate broad, opportunistic targeting of perimeter infrastructure rather than a single campaign.
lastChange: 2026-09-11 — MikroTik formally KEV-listed 10 Sep; Cisco FMC/Citrix NetScaler carry a 12 Sep federal patch deadline; sixth vendor family added this month.
orgRelevance: Confirm Cisco Firewall Management Center and Citrix NetScaler are patched or have a documented compensating control before 12 Sep; close out the MikroTik '-2' SSH-account hunt now that it is KEV-listed; verify asset inventory covers all six vendor families.

name: Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy / Zaporizhzhia
status: The 3-day Kyiv-Moscow capital-strike pause (tied to the Witkoff/Kushner envoy visit) lapsed on schedule 8 Sep with a mass Russian attack on Kyiv (166 drones, 32 cruise missiles, ballistic/anti-ship missiles) killing several and injuring dozens; NATO Sec-Gen Rutte says Ukrainian civilian deaths are at their highest level since May 2022. A separate, narrower 30-day energy-infrastructure-specific halt commitment from the 7 Sep Trump-Putin call remains unconfirmed as violated. ZNPP remains on restored external power (since 7 Sep).
importance: High — shapes European security and munitions/air-defense demand; the ZNPP dimension carries independent nuclear-safety significance.
assessment: The capital-strike pause's clean lapse (with a heavy resumed attack) confirms the base-case forecast from two cycles ago. The separate energy-infrastructure-specific halt's status is genuinely unresolved rather than disproven, since the 8 Sep targets (TV station, homes, school) were not specifically grid infrastructure — a distinction worth preserving rather than reading the lapse as a full ceasefire collapse.
lastChange: 2026-09-11 — ISW's 10 Sep assessment: Ukraine conducted its deepest-yet drone strike (~3,000km) against a major Russian gas complex; Russia struck 13 oblasts with 149 strike UAVs; a Russian drone entered Moldovan airspace during President Zelensky's departure from Chisinau (9 Sep); Polish PM Tusk said a border-crossing threat was prevented overnight. Neither incident specifically targeted grid infrastructure; the energy-halt question remains unresolved.
orgRelevance: Macro A&D demand context; no direct organizational action. ZNPP resolution and the new airspace-incursion pattern remain relevant to critical-infrastructure and airspace-security monitoring.
nextIndicator: A confirmed strike specifically on Ukrainian power/grid infrastructure (would resolve the energy-halt question); any further airspace-incursion incident; any further ZNPP power loss.

name: DoD AI Vendor Governance / Anthropic Dispute
status: DoD has rolled out custom ChatGPT and Grok instances on GenAI.mil to roughly 3 million personnel while Anthropic's Claude remains the sole major model excluded from the platform. Pentagon leadership has reaffirmed that removal of Anthropic's products from DoD systems will complete by the end of September, notwithstanding the 28 Aug district-court ruling against the underlying 'supply chain risk' designation; a second Anthropic suit remains pending before the D.C. Circuit (which previously denied a stay request).
importance: Medium — a precedent-relevant test of whether AI-vendor safety guardrails on autonomous-weapons/surveillance use cases can trigger adverse government procurement action, and whether a court ruling against such action restores market access while further litigation proceeds.
assessment: DoD is proceeding with its stated removal timeline independent of the district-court ruling and is now operationally further along (ChatGPT/Grok live, Claude absent), reinforcing that the department intends to keep litigating rather than concede the underlying dispute. The precedent remains relevant to any AI (or other) vendor navigating a similar guardrail-driven procurement dispute with a government customer.
lastChange: 2026-09-11 — no new legal filing or ruling identified this cycle; GenAI.mil rollout and month-end removal timeline both continue unchanged; standalone AI-governance bills show no confirmed floor action, with AI provisions continuing to move primarily via the FY26 NDAA.
orgRelevance: Relevant to organizations assessing DoD AI-vendor stability or considering similar safety-guardrail positions in government contracting; not a direct action item absent a specific GenAI.mil dependency.
nextIndicator: D.C. Circuit ruling on Anthropic's second suit; confirmation that removal completed by month-end.

name: Attritable-Systems Capture / Reverse-Engineering Risk (Anduril Dive-LD)
status: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy recovered a defective ('dead in the water') Anduril Dive-LD unmanned underwater vehicle near the Strait of Hormuz (~8-9 Sep). CENTCOM and Anduril state it carried no classified sonar/radar payload and no sensitive data; analysts (Defense News) expect Iran will attempt to reverse-engineer the low-cost, attritable hardware regardless.
importance: Medium — a live test of the attritable/expendable-systems design assumption that vehicle loss is an acceptable operational cost, distinct from (but adjacent to) the DIB's materials-chokepoint exposure.
assessment: A narrow, genuine technology-exposure event rather than a sensitive-data breach: the risk is hardware/manufacturing-technique insight an adversary can extract from physical capture, which is a distinct category from the data-loss risk vendors typically address. No evidence yet of Iranian technical disclosure derived from the unit.
lastChange: 2026-09-11 — thread opened following DefenseScoop/Defense News reporting on the capture and expected reverse-engineering effort.
orgRelevance: Firms fielding attritable/expendable autonomous hardware in contested environments should validate that 'no sensitive data' assurances also account for hardware-capture exposure, not just software/data-loss exposure.
nextIndicator: Any Iranian public disclosure of reverse-engineered Dive-LD components or derivative systems; independent confirmation of the 'no sensitive data' assessment; similar capture events involving other attritable US systems.
